notes: Reproduction successful. Product node converges to 100.00% validation accuracy at step 1,000 under sparse regime (p_e=1/N, N=16), exactly matching the paper claim in Section 5.2.4/Figure 6. No external datasets or pre-trained weights needed — all data is synthetically generated.
eval_output_format: JSON output in /repo/reproduce_3199_results.json with 'value' field containing validation accuracy percentage.
known_levers: Learning rate (0.02 from paper, sensitive); p_e sparsity probability (1/N is theoretically optimal); Gaussian weight initialization mean/std (0.5/0.25 default); batch size (100 from paper); number of parallel outputs n_outputs (250); seed (convergence to 100% is robust).
setup_notes: Container from docker.1ms.run/pytorch/pytorch:2.1.0-cuda12.1-cudnn8-runtime. PyTorch 2.1.0 works despite requirements.txt specifying 2.11.0. Python 3.10.13 works despite README requiring 3.12. No additional pip installs needed. All data is synthetic — no external downloads.

optimization_objective.summary: Maximize validation accuracy on 16-bit parity under sparse sampling, with convergence speed and sample efficiency as secondary goals. At N=16 baseline is already optimal; improvement means scaling to harder conditions while maintaining 100%.

metrics.name: Validation Accuracy
metrics.rationale: Primary paper metric. 100% means perfect generalization from sparse observations.

metrics.name: Convergence Steps
metrics.rationale: Steps to reach 100% accuracy. Faster convergence implies better optimization efficiency.

metrics.name: Coverage at Convergence
metrics.rationale: Fraction of truth table observed at convergence. Lower is better — stronger generalization.

optimization_objective.success_policy: Primary success: validation accuracy reaches 100%. Secondary improvements: faster convergence and lower coverage. If exploring higher N, find maximum N where 100% remains achievable. Regression below 95% at N=16 is failure.
